nodes.label: Should we raise our Pro plan…
nodes.description: Should we raise our Pro plan price from £49 to £59 a month?

provenance.reasoning: Connectivity repair wired this option to a factor another option targets; no effect value is implied

open_questions: The brief does not say whether your "MRR" goal covers the Pro plan only or MRR across all plans and revenue sources, so the model measures it for the Pro plan only. Which did you mean?
Does "MRR" get there within 12 months? The model holds the deadline; no result answers that yet.

Which option does better on "MRR"? Olumi reads "MRR" as depending on "Pro plan price" times "Paying subscribers". Olumi's analysis multiplies them when every part has a figure and together they match "MRR" (within 5%); otherwise it adds those effects up and cannot say which option does better on "MRR".
What is "Monthly churn" today? Your limit (less than 5%) can only be checked against Olumi's estimate of 3.5%, not a figure you gave, until you give yours.

Olumi estimated that raising "Monthly churn" by 1 point lowers "Paying subscribers" by 180 subscribers, which is more than the analysis can represent on the ranges these two are measured on, so it was not used: a placeholder stands in for it. How much does "Monthly churn" change "Paying subscribers"?

Olumi estimated that raising "New paying subscribers per month" by 1 subscriber/month raises "Paying subscribers" by 12 subscribers, which is more than the analysis can represent on the ranges these two are measured on, so it was not used: a placeholder stands in for it. How much does "New paying subscribers per month" change "Paying subscribers"?

Olumi estimated that raising "Pro plan price" by 1 GBP/month raises "MRR" by 1500 GBP/month, which is more than the analysis can represent on the ranges these two are measured on, so it was not used: a placeholder stands in for it. How much does "Pro plan price" change "MRR"?

Olumi estimated that raising "Paying subscribers" by 1 subscriber raises "MRR" by 50 GBP/month, which is more than the analysis can represent on the ranges these two are measured on, so it was not used: a placeholder stands in for it. How much does "Paying subscribers" change "MRR"?
Does “MRR” mean Pro-plan MRR only or MRR across all plans and revenue sources? The model provisionally measures the Pro plan only.

The stated £75k MRR does not exactly equal 1,500 paying subscribers at £49/month (£73.5k). Confirm whether this reflects other plans, add-ons, annual-plan monthly equivalents, discounts, or a different MRR scope.
Monthly churn is provisionally estimated at 3.5%; validate the current monthly churn rate before relying on the 5% constraint check.

The assumed price effects are provisional: each £1 increase is estimated to add 0.05 percentage points to monthly churn and reduce new paying subscribers by 0.5 per month. Validate these elasticities from historical pricing, conversion, and retention data.
New paying subscribers are provisionally estimated at 53 per month, approximately offsetting 3.5% churn on 1,500 subscribers. Confirm current acquisition and retention cohorts.

The 12-month subscriber effects assume a one-point increase in monthly churn reduces the year-end subscriber base by 180, while one additional new subscriber per month adds 12 to the year-end base; cohort retention and growth dynamics may differ.

Olumi reads "MRR" as "Pro plan price" and "Paying subscribers" multiplied together. Olumi's analysis multiplies them when every part has a figure and together they match "MRR" (within 5%); otherwise it adds up each effect separately. "Raise price to £59/month" and "Raise price to £54/month" can push "Pro plan price" and "Paying subscribers" in opposite directions, so whether "MRR" rises or falls depends on how large each change is — and adding the effects up can get even that direction wrong. If it adds them up, this model cannot show which option does better on "MRR": treat its figures then as a rough approximation, not a decision.
